legend: We start with a string s%%ZSMJ0%% consisting only of the digits 1%%ZSMJ1%%, 2%%ZSMJ2%%, or 3%%ZSMJ3%%. The length of s%%ZSMJ4%% is denoted by |s|%%ZSMJ5%%. For each i%%ZSMJ6%% from 1%%ZSMJ7%% to |s|%%ZSMJ8%%, the i%%ZSMJ9%%-th character of s%%ZSMJ10%% is denoted by si%%ZSMJ11%%.
There is one cursor. The cursor's location ℓ%%ZSMJ12%% is denoted by an integer in {0,…,|s|}%%ZSMJ13%%, with the following meaning:
If ℓ=0%%ZSMJ14%%, then the cursor is located before the first character of s%%ZSMJ15%%.
If ℓ=|s|%%ZSMJ16%%, then the cursor is located right after the last character of s%%ZSMJ17%%.
If 0<ℓ<|s|%%ZSMJ18%%, then the cursor is located between sℓ%%ZSMJ19%% and sℓ+1%%ZSMJ20%%.
We denote by sleft%%ZSMJ21%% the string to the left of the cursor and sright%%ZSMJ22%% the string to the right of the cursor.
We also have a string c%%ZSMJ23%%, which we call our clipboard, which starts out as empty. There are three types of actions:
The Move action. Move the cursor one step to the right. This increments ℓ%%ZSMJ24%% once.
The Cut action. Set c←sright%%ZSMJ25%%, then set s←sleft%%ZSMJ26%%.
The Paste action. Append the value of c%%ZSMJ27%% to the end of the string s%%ZSMJ28%%. Note that this doesn't modify c%%ZSMJ29%%.
The cursor initially starts at ℓ=0%%ZSMJ30%%. Then, we perform the following procedure:
Perform the Paste action sℓ%%ZSMJ31%% times.
If ℓ=x%%ZSMJ32%%, stop. Otherwise, return to step 1.

You're given the initial string s%%ZSMJ33%% and the integer x%%ZSMJ34%%. What is the length of s%%ZSMJ35%% when the procedure stops? Since this value may be very large, only find it modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ36%%.
It is guaranteed that ℓ≤|s|%%ZSMJ37%% at any time.
input: The first line of input contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ38%% (1≤t≤1000%%ZSMJ39%%) denoting the number of test cases. The next lines contain descriptions of the test cases.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer x%%ZSMJ40%% (1≤x≤106%%ZSMJ41%%). The second line of each test case consists of the initial string s%%ZSMJ42%% (1≤|s|≤500%%ZSMJ43%%). It is guaranteed, that s%%ZSMJ44%% consists of the characters "1", "2", "3".

It is guaranteed that the sum of x%%ZSMJ45%% in a single file is at most 106%%ZSMJ46%%. It is guaranteed that in each test case before the procedure will stop it will be true that ℓ≤|s|%%ZSMJ47%% at any time.
output: For each test case, output a single line containing a single integer denoting the answer for that test case modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ48%%.
